title: Kid Thomas's band, Raceland and Grand Isle
summary: During the war he and Mealy Bones played with Kid Thomas, who had plenty of work, including Saturday dances at Raceland; he also played Grand Isle for Tony.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: Was that during the last war or about when was the memory of that?

Yeah, well that was during the last war. Me and Mealy Bones was playing with him. Mealy was playing clarinet and I was playing sax. And Thomas had nice work. In fact he had more work than he could really do. Because we was going down by every Saturday around wrestling, playing for old man LeBlanc. That was a nickel dance too. The nickel dance was popular, you know what I mean, at that time. Especially all throughout the country. We only had a couple of them here in the city. But everywhere you went out of town to play for Whitey was nickel dance.
Where was that on Grand Isle? The theater?

Oh no, that's Raceland. Oh, Raceland over there. Yeah. Of course I went down to Grand Isle. I went down to Grand Isle and played for Tony in Marula. In fact, I was the first, one of the first colored bands went down and played for Tony when he went down there. Because we used to play for him up in Seussbury. He used to have a place up in Seussbury. And he decided to go down to buy, which I don't blame him because there wasn't nothing but money down there. He's a big gambler and he had the dance hall going and gambling and selling seafood and all like that. Well, he really was making his money. But Big Ike Roberson had a band. Me, Ike Roberson, George Lewis, the Albert Fernandez. We were playing with Big Ike Roberson for Tony in Seussbury. And quite naturally when he went down to buy, well, he still took us down there with him. And after I gave the band up, we still went down there. We used to use Frank Crump. Frank Crump on clarinet and sax and I'd play sax and Albert Fernandez on trumpet. And George Guido on banjo. We had a good lineup down there. We had been playing with dear
